hook: Written by The Great Hippo, this is built around an internal file that keeps throwing errors, with older revisions you can step back through one by one. The format is part of the story, so read each version slowly and compare them. It is a horror piece, but most of the dread comes from what changes between versions.
whyItMatters: It uses page structure itself to tell a story, here a revision history and a server error. Instead of announcing that something is wrong, it lets the document drift until you notice. The idea of a place that should not exist seeping into paperwork makes it a natural pick for readers who enjoy stories about untrustworthy records.
thingsToNotice:
Going backward in time, each revision gets more specific and more alarming: the island off Japan appears, the exclusion zone grows from ten to fifty kilometers, concrete-plugged stairwells lead to a complex more than several kilometers deep, and the redactions multiply. The oldest version flips the premise entirely, since it is staff, not files, who start calling the island Site-5 and walk down those stairs, and a 1989 examination of hundreds of recovered bodies found warped nervous systems and brains that had liquefied and bled out.

Note too that the cleanup bot's job shifts from sterilizing files to sterilizing people, and the camera feed that fails to load in newer versions finally plays in the oldest one. The last page offers a tidy explanation that it was all a software bug, patched in 2019. Then comes an email from J. Davis, the administrator whose address sits on every error notice, saying the explanation is a lie, the place is real, and he will see you there.
